name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. ---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

# Stand-in for the AI service and the error-report endpoint, on this Mac only.
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

LOG = open(sys.argv[2], 'a', buffering=1)

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def _log(self, body):
        LOG.write(json.dumps({'method': self.command, 'path': self.path, 'body': body[:4000]}) + '\n')

    def _send(self, status, payload, headers=()):
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(data)))
        for k, v in headers:
            self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        self._log('')
        if self.path.rstrip('/').endswith('/models'):
            self._send(200, {'object': 'list', 'data': [{'id': 'gpt-5.2', 'object': 'model', 'owned_by': 'openai'}]})
        else:
            self._send(404, {'error': {'message': 'not here', 'code': 'not_found'}})

    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length') or 0)).decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        self._log(body)
        if self.path.rstrip('/').endswith('/responses'):
            self._send(400, {'error': {'message': 'Invalid value for input[3].content: stand-in refusal for the live check.',
                                       'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'input', 'code': 'invalid_value'}},
                       [('x-request-id', 'req_standin_400')])
        else:
            self._send(200, {})

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass

ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
PY

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

# Error-handling sweep: trial findings

This file is the result of a reading-only sweep. It checks JusPrin's AI chat and Home code, and the JusPrin Cloud server's v2 code, against the trial copy of the error-handling rules and the `error-handling` audit skill. Nothing was built, run, changed or committed.

What was read:
- **Desktop app:** every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` at commit `5e173c5e15`.
- **Server:** every `.py` under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` except `tests/` and `migrations/`, at `2086b2ec64` in tsd-enterprise.

How it was judged:
- An outcome counts as decided by a person only if its cause is in `expected-errors-app.cpp` or `expected-errors-server.py`.
- Every other outcome counts as an unexpected error.

How to read the locations:
- Line numbers are from those two commits.
- App paths start at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths start at `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- "Confirmed" means I read the code myself. Several findings were first reported by a reader subagent and then confirmed by me.
- Nothing was confirmed by running code.

## 1. Findings, most harmful first

### 1. In the desktop app, no failure is ever reported, and a thrown one reaches OrcaSlicer's generic handler
- **Where:**
  - The entry-point handler is `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:926-947` (`on_page_message`). It catches `json::exception`, adds the message type and id, and rethrows. That part is allowed.
  - The rethrow, and every other throw from the chat page, the timer pumps, Home's page messages (`Home/HomeHost.cpp:161`), Home's `CallAfter` bodies (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:749`, `:769-785`, `:851-863`, `:1371-1378`) and the tool pump (`ShellController.cpp:337-339`, which has no try), all end in `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` → `generic_exception_handle` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:855-909`, `:9600-9604`).
  - Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ calls a reporting function.
- **What the code does:** OrcaSlicer's handler writes a log line and queues `wxLogError("OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception: %1%")` with the exception text, then rethrows with `throw;`. The comment at `AgentHost.cpp:931-934` says this handler "logs it and reports it once". It does not report.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone hits a bug, for example a page message missing a field, or Home asking for an unknown sign-in link (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:740`). They see an Orca-branded error that holds internal text such as "jusprin-agent-bridge: … ". Nothing reaches JusPrin. My inference, not run: because the handler rethrows, the app then quits.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler and report. Medium that the app quits.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 2. A model list whose shape changes crashes the app, because parsing throws on OrcaSlicer's HTTP thread
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:43-62`: `on_complete` calls `parse_model_list`.
  - `Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:177-188`: it reads `response.at("data")`, `model.at("id").get<std::string>()`, `model.at("format")` and `model.at("credits").get<int>()`.
  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:796-801`: `perform()` runs `http_perform` on a `std::thread`. At `:519-526` that thread calls `completefn` directly, with no try around it.
- **What the code does:** If one model entry has no `format`, or its `credits` is not an integer, a `json` exception leaves a `std::thread` body. That calls `std::terminate`.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure…". The HTTP callback is an entry point with no handler. Keeping the parser strict is right; what is missing is the handler at the top.
- **What goes wrong:** One field changed on JusPrin Cloud, or in a provider's model list, makes the app quit each time it fetches models. That happens at launch and at sign-in. Nothing is reported.
- **Confidence:** high, by reading.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 3. An AI-request status the table does not name is shown as a network problem, and every 5xx as "temporarily unavailable"
- **Where:** `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:667-699` (`http_error`).
- **What the code does:** It sorts statuses by fixed rules and ends in `network_error`, "The AI request could not reach the … service.", with Retry. That last line catches:
  - 400, 404, 405, 409, 410 and 422;
  - 402 from any provider other than JusPrin's account;
  - any status other than 408 that came with no curl text.

  Any status of 500 or above other than 529 becomes `service_unavailable`. That includes JusPrin Cloud's own 502 `upstream_error` and 500 tracebacks. Because the `>= 500` test comes before the timeout test, the gateway's 504 `timeout` never becomes `timeout`. A 402 from JusPrin Cloud that is not `credits_exhausted` still becomes "You're out of credits." (`:683-685`). 401 and 403 always mean the sign-in ended or the key was rejected (`:673-674`, `:686-687`).
- **Rules broken:**
  - "A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause."
  - "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - JusPrin Cloud refuses the app's own request with 400 `invalid_request`, which is a bug on one of our two ends. The person is told to check their network and Retry, which never helps. Nobody hears of it.
  - Someone's OpenAI key cannot use the model they typed, and OpenAI answers 404. They get the same network sentence. Key setup takes the same path (`Agent/AgentSetup.cpp:112-127`).
  - A gateway fault reads as a provider outage.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 4. An error event inside the reply stream loses its code, so even causes the table names are shown as a generic failure
- **Where:** `Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:176-177` and `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:404-405`. Both turn any `error` or `response.failed` event into `agent_service_error`, "The AI service could not complete the response.", and drop the event's code and message.

- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** These failures, three of which have table entries, show as the same generic line with Retry:

  - the gateway's own mid-stream `timeout` (table: `timeout`);
  - the gateway's `upstream_error` (a gateway fault that should be reported).

  The saved message keeps only `agent_service_error`.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 5. Server: a reply that ends with the provider's own error event is recorded as completed, and its chat is kept as completed
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:301-307`: `self.outcome = 'completed'` is set whenever the upstream line iterator ends, whatever the last event was.
  - `stream.py:49-52` (Anthropic) and `:67-73` (Responses): an upstream `error` event, or a `response.error`, is rewritten to `STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE` and forwarded, and the loop carries on.
  - `stream.py:100-109`: an unterminated last event is dropped without a word.
  - `gateway.py:241`: `keep()` then keeps the chat for fine-tuning as a completed reply.
  - `_log` (`gateway.py:330-361`) records outcome `completed` in Langfuse.
  - Nothing reports it.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." (The sentence is "The model service failed while answering.")
- **What goes wrong:** When a provider fails mid-reply, the person sees a failure. The Langfuse record says completed. The kept chat, which is training data, holds a failed reply marked as complete. Nobody can count these failures.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 6. Server: upstream refusals are interpreted and given sentences of their own; only 401, 403 and 404 reach Sentry, and the provider's error text is dropped
- **Where:**

455	## 3. The rules and the skill: what was unclear, missing or contradictory, and what I did
456	
457	1. **The worktree was not at the stated commit.** The brief said it should be at `5e173c5e15`. It was at `ff318b33bc`, two commits behind. Six in-scope files differ: `ProjectPersistence.cpp/.hpp`, `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp/.hpp` and two others. The brief forbids switching or pulling. So I extracted the in-scope folders at `5e173c5e15` with `git archive` into the session's scratch folder and read that copy. All app line numbers are from `5e173c5e15`. After the sweep, the session that started this one said to run `git checkout --detach 5e173c5e15`. I did, and HEAD is now `5e173c5e15`. A `diff -rq` shows that the copy I read is identical to the checked-out `Agent/` and `Home/` folders, so the findings stand unchanged.
458	2. **The shared notes folder.** It held one sibling note, `error-handling-enforcement.md`. The session instructions say to read sibling notes, but the brief says the trial must not know the earlier history. I did not open the note, so the trial stays independent.
459	3. **The app table covers only failures of a request to the AI.** By the brief, everything else is unexpected. That includes outcomes that plainly were designed:
460	   - "already reported" for a print report;
461	   - attachment too large or of an unsupported type;
462	   - wrong code and wrong password at sign-in;
463	   - a file from the other app with no version;
464	   - rejected tool calls fed back to the model.
465	
466	   I reported the code that handles them as findings only where it also drops detail, invents a cause, or records a failure as a success. I ranked the clearly designed product refusals low and grouped them. Whether they need table entries is a decision for Kenneth.
467	4. **Tool results go to the model, not to the person.** The rules say the top handler "tells the person". For a tool call the caller is the model or an outside client. The rules don't say:
468	   - whether a tool failure should end the turn and show the person "Something went wrong on our side";
469	   - whether the tool error contract (`invalid_arguments`, `stale_workspace`, `busy`) counts as expected errors that need table entries.
470	
471	   The tool reader treated the model's own correctable mistakes as normal protocol answers, and reported only failures inside the app and states that cannot happen. I kept that split.
472	5. **"Keep the other side's error text" conflicts with privacy.** The server drops the provider's body on purpose (`gateway.py:321`, "an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The app's test `tests/agent/test_provider_agent.cpp:582-600` asserts that the body is not kept ("safe errors"). The rules give no exception. I followed the rules and reported it (findings 3 and 6), and noted the stated reason.
473	6. **"A status code is not a cause" against how the table is used.** The app table's causes ("rate limited", "overloaded", "unavailable") are reached in the code only through status codes (`http_error`). The rule forbids a status code as a cause but doesn't say how a status may be mapped to a named cause. I accepted the mapping where the status means that cause (429 → rate limited, 529 → overloaded). I flagged the catch-all branches (finding 3).
474	7. **Compatibility defaults for stored files.** Several readers of stored files deliberately read an unknown value from a newer build as a default ("A state a newer build added reads as complete", `ProjectStateDocument.cpp:88-91`, and the StoredFormat comments). The rules say a message our own code cannot read is unexpected, and say nothing about forward compatibility. I reported only the defaults that change meaning (role to Assistant, action class to ReadOnly), and ranked them medium.
475	8. **What counts as an entry point in a wx app with threads.** The rules say "the top of each entry point". I took that to mean:
476	   - each wx event handler, timer and `CallAfter` body, all of which end in OrcaSlicer's main-loop handler;
477	   - each HTTP callback, which runs on its own thread with no handler at all (finding 2).
478	9. **The order of the rules matters.** "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot" assumes the top handler exists. Today a throw ends in OrcaSlicer's generic handler, which my reading suggests ends the app. If the throws were added before the handler, recoverable mistakes would become crashes. The brief says to judge as if the handler existed, so I did. I note here that the rules give no order for the work.
479	10. **"Each occurrence is counted"** doesn't say where or how. The trial table's `count_expected` writes a log line, which the rules say "reaches nobody". I reported that nothing counts at these commits (finding 28), and did not judge the log-line counter.
480	11. **Skill step 5 can't be fully applied.** Step 5 says to flag a table entry with no test, or with no quote of Kenneth's yes in its commit message. Neither table exists at these commits, and tests were out of scope. I checked only the entries' causes. On the server, `invalid_request`, `unknown_model`, `method_not_allowed` and `upstream_error` are correctly listed as unexpected. `quota_exhausted` exists in `errors.py` with no table entry (finding 30).
481	12. **Skill step 4's "follow one failure up from each entry point the change touches"** means every entry point when the whole code counts as changed. Each reader followed one failure from each kind of entry point: page message, timer, HTTP callback, tool call, web-view load, ASGI request and Django view. They did not follow one from every handler.
482	13. **Skill: "Do not search for particular code shapes."** All functions were read. I used text search only to find callers and catch sites I had already read, for example the callers of `read_attachment_blob`.

484	15. **Briefing mechanics.** The readers were told to write their results to files. The harness refuses report files from subagents, so they returned the text instead. Nothing was lost.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

"""The gateway's own error answers, and the expected-errors table.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}}, never bytes
from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed out", so 401 means only that
the person's own token was missing or rejected. credits_exhausted adds what the
client needs to offer a way on, beside "error"; update_required adds
minimumVersion, the oldest release still served.

An error is expected only when a person decided what the product does for that
named cause; EXPECTED holds those decisions. Every other failure is unexpected:
nothing handles it where it happens, the one handler at the top of the endpoint
reports it, and the app is told UNEXPECTED_CODE with UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE.

## Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

## Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

## Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

## Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.

"""How the gateway answers when the model provider or the gateway itself fails,
through the real ASGI application (routing, sign-in, credits, real Redis), with
a fake provider that answers the way Anthropic and OpenAI document, and a
stand-in Sentry on this machine that receives what the real Sentry SDK sends.

A chat too large for the provider is the one provider failure the person can
do something about: it is answered with its own code and words and reaches no
Sentry. Every other failure reaches Sentry once, from the one handler at the
top of the endpoint, with the provider's status, request id and error text
and what is known of the request, and the app is told only "Something went
wrong on our side". Neither is ever recorded as a completed reply, nor kept
as one."""
import gzip
import json
from unittest import mock

import brotli
import httpx
import sentry_sdk
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.test import Client, RequestFactory, override_settings

class FailureTestCase(GatewayTestCase):
    """GatewayTestCase with a stand-in Sentry and a record of every Langfuse
    generation and every kept chat."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.sentry = FakeSentry()
        previous = sentry_sdk.get_client()
        sentry_sdk.init(dsn=self.sentry.dsn, default_integrations=False, send_client_reports=False,
                        auto_session_tracking=False)
        self.addCleanup(self.sentry.close)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: sentry_sdk.get_global_scope().set_client(previous))
        self.addCleanup(sentry_sdk.flush)
        patch_attr(self, gateway.os, 'environ', {**gateway.os.environ, 'LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY': 'pk-test'})
        self.langfuse = patch_attr(self, gateway, 'get_client', mock.MagicMock())
        self.kept = patch_attr(self, gateway._Turn, '_keep_sync', mock.MagicMock())

    def events(self):
        """The events that reached the stand-in Sentry."""
        sentry_sdk.flush()
        events = []
        for _, headers, body in self.sentry.received:
            if headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'gzip':
                body = gzip.decompress(body)
            elif headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'br':
                body = brotli.decompress(body)
            events += [item.payload.json for item in Envelope.deserialize(body).items if item.type == 'event']
        return events

    def reported(self):
        """The one report, as one line: the exception's type and text."""
        events = self.events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1, events)
        exception = events[0]['exception']['values'][-1]
        return f'{exception["type"]}: {exception["value"]}'

    def outcomes(self):
        return [call.kwargs['metadata']['outcome'] for call in self.langfuse.return_value.start_observation.call_args_list]

    def counted(self):
        return [call.kwargs for call in self.langfuse.return_value.start_observation.call_args_list]

    async def post_chat(self, path, body, **kwargs):
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER='jusprin-chats'):
            return await self.post(path, body, chat=CHAT, **kwargs)

    def assert_unexpected_answer(self, response):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 500, response.text)
        self.assertEqual(response.json(), UNEXPECTED_ANSWER)
        self.assertNotIn(REQUEST_ID, response.text)

    def assert_unexpected_event(self, response):
        """A stream whose last event is the gateway's unexpected answer."""
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        last = parse_sse(response.text)[-1]
        self.assertEqual(last['type'], 'error')
        code = last['error']['code'] if 'error' in last else last['code']
        message = last['error']['message'] if 'error' in last else last['message']
        self.assertEqual((code, message), ('server_error', 'Something went wrong on our side'))

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report of an unexpected error in the
JusPrin desktop app, passed on to the app's Sentry project.

The app sends one only when the person pressed "Report to JusPrin team" or
turned automatic reports on. A report is anonymous: no token is read, and the
body holds only the fields below, the same lines the app's dialog shows under
"See what the report contains".

The Sentry project is the desktop app's own, apart from the server's; its DSN
comes from JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. The report is sent to Sentry before the
app is answered, so the app hears "reported" only once Sentry has it. A server
without the DSN, or a Sentry that refuses the report, fails the request like
any other fault of the server, and the server's own Sentry hears about it.
So does a body the app could not have sent.
"""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import requests
from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.http import JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST
from sentry_sdk.consts import EndpointType
from sentry_sdk.envelope import Envelope
from sentry_sdk.utils import Dsn

# The fields of a report and the longest text each may hold. "where" is the
# stack, from the app's own pages only for now; empty when there is none.
FIELDS = {
    'app': 200,       # "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)"
    'os': 200,        # "macOS 26.3"
    'doing': 500,     # what the app was doing, in the app's words
    'error': 8000,    # the error as it reached the top, the other side's text included
    'where': 32000,
}
MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024


def _event(report: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        'event_id': uuid.uuid4().hex,
        'timestamp': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'level': 'error',
        'platform': 'javascript' if report['where'] else 'native',
        'logger': 'jusprin.app',
        'release': report['app'],
        'message': {'formatted': report['error']},
        'tags': {'doing': report['doing'][:200], 'os': report['os'][:200]},
        'extra': {'doing': report['doing'], 'where': report['where']},
        # One issue per error and what the app was doing, whatever the stack.
        'fingerprint': [report['doing'], report['error']],
    }


def _send_to_sentry(event: dict) -> None:
    dsn = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN
    if not dsn:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured('JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN is not set, so app error reports cannot be passed on')
    auth = Dsn(dsn).to_auth('jusprin-server')
    envelope = Envelope(headers={'event_id': event['event_id']})
    envelope.add_event(event)
    response = requests.post(auth.get_api_url(EndpointType.ENVELOPE), data=envelope.serialize(),
                             headers={'X-Sentry-Auth': auth.to_header(), 'Content-Type': 'application/x-sentry-envelope'},
                             timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def error_reports(request):
    # Our own app is the only sender, so a body it could not have sent is the
    # server's unexpected error: the request fails, and the server's own
    # Sentry hears about it.
    if len(request.body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f'an app error report of {len(request.body)} bytes is over the {MAX_BODY_BYTES} the app may send')
    report = json.loads(request.body)
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(FIELDS) or not all(
            isinstance(report[name], str) and len(report[name]) <= limit for name, limit in FIELDS.items()) \
            or not report['error'] or not report['doing']:
        raise ValueError('an app error report does not have the fields the app sends')
    event = _event(report)
    _send_to_sentry(event)
    return JsonResponse({'id': event['event_id']})

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report from the desktop app reaches
Sentry before the app is answered, and nothing else is passed on."""
import json
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

import requests
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports'
REPORT = {
    'app': 'JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)',
    'os': 'macOS 26.3',
    'doing': 'exporting G-code from Home',
    'error': "std::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: in copy_file: Permission denied [\"/tmp/a\"] [\"/tmp/b\"]",
    'where': '',
}


class FakeSentry:
    """A Sentry that keeps what it is sent, and answers with `status`."""

    def __init__(self, status=200):
        self.received = []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def do_POST(self):
                fake.received.append((self.path, dict(self.headers), self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))))
                self.send_response(status)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(b'{}')

            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.dsn = f'http://publickey@127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}/16'

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

    def event(self):
        path, headers, body = self.received[-1]
        items = body.split(b'\n')
        return path, headers, json.loads(items[2])

    def test_a_page_stack_goes_with_the_report(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry()
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        stack = 'TypeError: x is undefined\n    at render (index.js:1:200)'
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn):
            self.assertEqual(self.post({**REPORT, 'where': stack}).status_code, 200)
        event = sentry.event()[2]
        self.assertEqual(event['extra']['where'], stack)
        self.assertEqual(event['platform'], 'javascript')

    def test_a_report_sentry_refuses_is_a_failure_not_an_answer(self):
